eli5.text: The CLI interface has been refactored to reduce unnecessary screen redraws, especially during streaming responses. MessageBlock now splits its content rendering into a separate memoized component, and AgentBranchItem uses standard React composition with children instead of content props. Additionally, the debugging hook now checks for the 'dev' environment instead of development mode. These changes make the interface feel smoother and reduce flickering when content updates, particularly noticeable when watching agent responses stream in real-time.

ai.title: Refine agent orchestration prompt constraints
ai.summary: Updated base2.ts to enforce sequential spawning for editor and context agents, removing parallel edit directives. Editor prompts in editor-best-of-n.ts now explicitly state the agent cannot read files independently. This clarifies dependency handling and prevents premature parallel execution of context-gathering and implementation steps.

eli5.text: The assistant now handles its helper steps in a stricter order instead of doing several at once. When it calls in specialized sub-agents to gather context and then edit code, the later edit step no longer starts until the context-gathering step is finished, which prevents the two from running side by side before the needed information is ready. You wouldn't see this directly, but you may notice the assistant takes a steadier, step-by-step path through tasks that involve reading files and then making changes, rather than jumping ahead. These prompt adjustments are internal wiring, so there's no new button or setting to use; it's simply how the assistant plans and runs those helper steps.

ai.summary: Refactor useConnectionStatus hook to replace fixed 30s setInterval with adaptive setTimeout polling. Interval increases from 10s to 10min based on consecutive successful health checks, resetting on failure. Scope limited to cli/src/hooks/use-connection-status.ts.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant through the command line, it no longer checks for a live connection every 30 seconds no matter what. Instead, it starts by checking within 10 seconds, and after several successful checks in a row it gradually waits longer between checks, 30 seconds, then a minute, then up to ten minutes, so it stops poking the server when everything is calm. The moment a check fails, it snaps back to checking every 10 seconds until things look healthy again. If you watch the logs, you would actually see messages noting when the wait gets longer or shorter, so the CLI now adapts how often it listens to the server based on whether the connection keeps looking good.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant, it no longer does all the setup work at once before showing anything. Instead, it prepares things behind the scenes using a step-by-step process that runs before the main interface appears. If you were watching the startup, you might notice the interface still appears normally, but the internal preparation is now split into cleaner, reusable pieces, like separating the theme setup from the authentication checks.

ai.title: Harden shell detection and OSC guard
ai.summary: New `detect-shell.ts` utility identifies shells via environment variables or parent process inspection, caching results to support PowerShell theme detection. OSC terminal detection logic is restored in `terminal-color-detection.ts` and `theme-system.ts`, guarded by a new `terminalSupportsOSC` check in `cli/src/index.tsx` to prevent hangs in non-supporting terminals. Windows PowerShell background color detection is added to `theme-system.ts`, prioritizing `(Get-Host).UI.RawUI.BackgroundColor` over generic system theme checks. `packages/internal/src/env.ts` suppresses environment logging during OSC detection subprocesses by checking `process.argv` for `--internal-osc-detect`.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant in a terminal, it now asks your terminal a quick yes/no question to check whether the terminal supports special color commands before trying to use them, which prevents the program from freezing on terminals that don't understand those commands. It also gets better at figuring out which kind of command prompt (like PowerShell, bash, or zsh) you're using by checking your system settings, so it can correctly detect whether you're on a dark or light theme, especially if you use PowerShell on Windows. These updates apply to anyone running the assistant from a command-line terminal today.

ai.summary: OpenAI-compatible v5 provider code forked into `packages/internal/src/openai-compatible`. Adds chat and completion modules with message conversion, finish-reason mapping, and metadata extraction. Implements `LanguageModelV2` spec via `openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts`. Supports structured outputs, tool calls, and image URL/base64 data handling.

eli5.text: The AI assistant can now work with a wider range of model providers right out of the box, without needing each one to be programmed in individually. Behind the scenes, the team copied and adapted the code that connects to OpenAI-style services into a shared internal toolkit, adding support for conversations, image inputs, structured responses, and usage tracking. If you looked closely, you'd see the system now understands extra details from each response (like which model was used or why it stopped) and can handle both full replies all at once and streamed responses chunk by chunk. This change appears to be live today and affects internal systems that rely on pluggable model providers.

ai.title: Remove single-text cache split in message converters
ai.summary: Removed logic splitting single-text user messages into cache-controlled fragments in convertCbToModelMessages and provider-specific converters (OpenAI-compatible, OpenRouter). This ensures messages are passed as unified content parts, preventing unintended cache control application on split text. Scope covers common/src/util/messages.ts and packages/internal chat converters. SDK llm.ts now imports OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel from @codebuff/internal/openai-compatible/index.

eli5.text: When you send a single message to the assistant, the system used to chop that message into two pieces: a short first part and a longer second part, in order to control how the provider cached the message. Now the whole message is sent as one piece instead, so the caching rules apply to the message as a whole and not to just the last chunk of text. If you send a plain message to a connected model, you no longer need to worry about your message being unexpectedly split into fragments behind the scenes. The SDK now also pulls in the model connector it needs directly from its own internal package instead of from the external source. This change is live today.
